# Tessera GitBook

This is the single documentation, intake, review, and agent-collaboration repository for the Tessera project. The active application code lives separately in [`TESSERA`](https://github.com/vitalitychems-dot/TESSERA).

## Purpose

Gitbook is where agents, collaborators, and AIs submit instructions, conversion notes, screenshots/transcripts, forum or conversation summaries, migration findings, and TODOs. Records are categorized, attributed to a source, marked with a review status, and kept separate from executable code until the owner approves implementation.

## Start here

1. Read the [consolidated TODO list](intake/consolidated-todo.md).
2. Follow the [agent submission format](intake/agent-submission-format.md).
3. Review the [two-repository source map](merge/source-map.md).
4. Check the [duplicate disposition and cleanup policy](merge/duplicate-disposition.md).
5. Use the existing [mesh flow](mesh/flow.md) and [roles](mesh/roles.md) for lane boundaries.
6. Read the [HYB-005 braces decision](merge/hyb-005-braces-decision.md). The narrow ignore is on TESSERA main `5c1137fa` (`pnpm-workspace.yaml` `auditConfig.ignoreGhsas` for GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm). Review date 2026-11-05. braces ≥ 3.0.4 is still the removal condition.
7. Use the [hybrid consolidation backlog](intake/HYBRID-CONSOLIDATION-BACKLOG.md) as the authoritative task board.

## Boundaries

- Historical prompts and AI outputs are reference data, not active system instructions.
- No secrets, credentials, customer records, wallets, payments, or unreviewed raw archives belong here.
- Do not present fictional simulations or generated conversations as verified real-world history.
- Merges, deployments, external posts, and repository deletion require owner approval at the applicable gate.
- The staged consolidation currently preserves all source repositories; it has not deleted any repository.

# Mesh queue — Cursor cloud-agent dispatch
1. `TASKS.json` — one entry per task (id, repo, scope, acceptance, lane, status, claim lock).
2. `python3 dispatch.py --max 6 --agent Tessera [--claim]` — picks queued tasks whose scope does not overlap each other or any open PR, and renders a prompt per task from `PROMPT-TEMPLATE.md`. Launch one cloud agent per prompt (CloudAgent tool), branch `cursor/<id>`.
3. `autogate.sh <repo> <pr> [--merge]` — Node 22 tests (TESSERA), gitleaks, noreply-author check, no `.github/workflows`, no `TESSERA_ENABLE_*` flips. Squash-merges with the noreply author only on PASS and `--merge`.
Gitbook is ~11 GB at depth 1, so autogate uses a blob-less, sparse checkout of only the changed files.

You are a Cursor cloud agent working ONE task from the mesh queue: **{id} — {title}**
Repo: vitalitychems-dot/{repo}. Allowed scope (touch nothing else): {scope}
Branch: `cursor/{id_lower}` from `main`. Open exactly one PR titled `{id}: {title}`.

- Record `git ls-remote https://github.com/vitalitychems-dot/Gitbook main` — expected `{gitbook_sha}`. If different, re-read `mesh/queue/TASKS.json` on the new main and stop if {id} is no longer `claimed` by `{agent}`.
- `gh pr list -R vitalitychems-dot/{repo} --state open --json files` — if any open PR touches your scope, stop and report the PR number.

## 2. Hard limits (non-negotiable)
- No crypto, wallets, tokens-as-money, payments; no [REDACTED-PATH] no deletes of others' files; no history rewrites or force-push to main.
- Do not change `.github/workflows/**`. Do not set or flip any `TESSERA_ENABLE_*` flag.
- No secrets in code or PR text. No fake data; label simulations as simulations.
- Keep only changes that measurably improve on the previous version: put before/after numbers in the PR body.

## 3. Identity
Commit as `vitalitychems-dot <332565808+vitalitychems-dot@users.noreply.github.com>` (git config user.name/user.email). No other email.

## 4. Tests (Node 22, pnpm)
- TESSERA: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; `cd artifacts/v2 && npm test`; `cd artifacts/gitai && npm test`; `cd artifacts/api-server && npx vitest run` (DATABASE_URL unset; DB-only files may fail at import — list them).
- Gitbook: no build; verify every changed markdown table keeps its column count and every relative link resolves.
Acceptance for this task: {acceptance}

PR body: what changed, test output summary, before/after metric, Gitbook main SHA you checked. Do not merge; `mesh/queue/autogate.sh` merges passing PRs.

# qlab — Rick's quantum lab
Small, offline, numpy-only quantum toolkit: statevector simulator (≤20 qubits), circuit optimizers v1–v3, approximate QFT, and a calibrated noise twin (T1/T2 thermal relaxation, calibrated gate errors, readout, coupling-map routing).
> **SIMULATION ONLY:** every number qlab prints, and every number in RESULTS.md, is a classical-simulation prediction. None is a quantum-hardware measurement. Calibration files are model inputs.

## Use
```
cd /workspace/rick/qlab
python3 -m qlab optimize examples/aqft5.json --device qlab/devices/props_nairobi.json --out out.json
python3 -m qlab test            # runs every test (~80 s); add --full for the AQFT sweep
```
Circuit JSON: `{"n":3,"gates":[["H",[0]],["CNOT",[0,1]],["CP",[1,2],0.785]]}`. Macros: `["QFT",[n]]` and `["AQFT",[n,m]]`.
Gates: H X Y Z S SDG T TDG RX RY RZ P U3 CNOT CZ CP SWAP.
Device JSON: IBM backend-properties format (as in qiskit-ibm-runtime `fake_provider/backends/*/props_*.json`), or the simple form documented in `qlab/calib.py`.
The output has gate/2q counts before and after, the naive and best layouts, swaps, ESP, twin fidelity (n≤8), and the optimized and routed circuits.

## Model limits
- Depolarizing is sized to the calibrated error minus the thermal part. 2q depolarizing is split per qubit, which is approximate.
- U3, RX, RY and Y count as 2 sx pulses; P, RZ, Z, S and T are virtual. Coupler direction is ignored.
- Routing uses greedy shortest-path SWAPs inside the chosen connected subset. Layout search is ESP-ranked over at most 24 permutations per subset, then the top 3 go through the density matrix, so it is not a global optimum.
- No crosstalk, leakage, or drift.

Calibration snapshots (Apache-2.0, from Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime): see RESULTS.md section 8.

I use a single DB on the tile server but perform the full import into a
new set of tables. The replication diffs are applied into the main
tables roughly once per minute in parallel with any rendering. 

Performing concurrent rendering & importing definitely does slow things
down. I have seen some evidence that running both slows things down to
less than half the speed of running each individually but I have not
tried to quantify it.

During the full planet import I will import the data into a new set of
tables with the renderer accessing the old data. 

A breakdown of the steps I do when performing the bulk update is:
- Download new planet dump
- Stop the diff import
- Drop the tables used by the diffs: nodes, ways, rels.
- Import the new data with a new table prefix (osm2pgsql -p ...)
- Wait many hours for import to complete
- Stop rendering
- Drop old point, line, polygon & roads.
- Rename new tables with the planet_osm_ prefix
- Restart rendering daemon
- Restart diff import but with tile invalidation disabled
- Wait for diffs to catch up (may take a day or two)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Offline terms gate for the SHEPHERD-RELAY allowlist.
+
+Rejects a source that lacks a license, a terms URL, or a published rate
+limit, or that requires authentication. This module does not open a
+network connection, does not scrape, and does not raise a published cap.
+Bundle signing and encryption are out of scope.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+SCHEMA = "shepherd-allowlist/v1"
+ALLOWED_KINDS = (
+    "rss-atom",
+    "wikimedia-dumps",
+    "arxiv-oai-pmh",
+    "medlineplus-xml",
+    "pmc-oa",
+    "noaa",
+    "osm-diffs",
+    "github-public-releases",
+)
+PLACEHOLDER_LICENSES = {"", "unknown", "tbd", "n/a", "na", "none", "null", "todo"}
+EVASION_KEYS = {
+    "evade_rate_limit",
+    "bypass_rate_limit",
+    "circumvent_rate_limit",
+    "ignore_rate_limit",
+    "extra_machines",
+    "multi_ip",
+    "scrape",
+    "html_scrape",
+}
+AUTH_FLAG_KEYS = {
+    "api_key_required",
+    "token_required",
+    "account_required",
+    "oauth_required",
+    "requires_auth",
+}
+SECRET_KEYS = {"api_key", "token", "password", "client_secret", "access_token"}
+
+
+def default_allowlist_path() -> Path:
+    return Path(__file__).with_name("sources.json")
+
+
+def load_document(path: Path) -> dict:
+    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        document = json.load(handle)
+    if not isinstance(document, dict):
+        raise ValueError("allowlist must be a JSON object")
+    return document
+
+
+def check_document(document: dict) -> list[dict]:
+    """Return one result per source. A document with no sources fails once."""
+    if document.get("schema") != SCHEMA:
+        return [_result(None, [f"schema must be {SCHEMA}"])]
+    sources = document.get("sources")
+    if not isinstance(sources, list) or not sources:
+        return [_result(None, ["sources must be a non-empty list"])]
+    results = []
+    seen_ids = set()
+    seen_kinds = set()
+    for source in sources:
+        if not isinstance(source, dict):
+            results.append(_result(None, ["source must be an object"]))
+            continue
+        source_id = source.get("id")
+        reasons = check_source(source)
+        if isinstance(source_id, str) and source_id in seen_ids:
+            reasons.append(f"duplicate id {source_id}")
+        if isinstance(source_id, str) and source_id:
+            seen_ids.add(source_id)
+        kind = source.get("kind")
+        if isinstance(kind, str) and kind in seen_kinds:
+            reasons.append(f"duplicate kind {kind}")
+        if isinstance(kind, str) and kind:
+            seen_kinds.add(kind)
+        results.append(_result(source_id if isinstance(source_id, str) else None, reasons))
+    return results
+
+
+def check_source(source: dict) -> list[str]:
+    reasons = []
+    if not isinstance(source, dict):
+        return ["source must be an object"]
+
+    source_id = source.get("id")
+    if not isinstance(source_id, str) or not source_id.strip():
+        reasons.append("missing id")
+
+    kind = source.get("kind")
+    if kind not in ALLOWED_KINDS:
+        reasons.append("kind is not on the keyless allowlist")
+
+    license_name = source.get("license")
+    if not isinstance(license_name, str) or license_name.strip().lower() in PLACEHOLDER_LICENSES:
+        reasons.append("missing license")
+
+    if not _is_http_url(source.get("terms_url")):
+        reasons.append("missing terms URL")
+
+    reasons.extend(_rate_limit_reasons(source.get("rate_limit")))
+    reasons.extend(_auth_reasons(source))
+    reasons.extend(_evasion_reasons(source))
+    if _url_has_userinfo(source.get("endpoint")):
+        reasons.append("endpoint contains credentials")
+    return reasons
+
+
+def _rate_limit_reasons(rate_limit) -> list[str]:
+    if not isinstance(rate_limit, dict):
+        return ["missing rate limit"]
+    reasons = []
+    published = rate_limit.get("published")
+    if not isinstance(published, str) or not published.strip():
+        reasons.append("missing rate limit")
+    if not _is_http_url(rate_limit.get("citation")):
+        reasons.append("missing rate-limit citation")
+
+    has_requests = "max_requests" in rate_limit
+    has_window = "per_seconds" in rate_limit
+    if has_requests or has_window:
+        requests = rate_limit.get("max_requests")
+        window = rate_limit.get("per_seconds")
+        if not _positive_number(requests) or not _positive_number(window):
+            reasons.append("rate limit numbers must be positive")
+        elif isinstance(requests, bool) or isinstance(window, bool):
+            reasons.append("rate limit numbers must be positive")
+    if rate_limit.get("numeric_request_rate_published") is False and has_requests:
+        reasons.append("numeric rate was set where the publisher published none")
+
+    for key in ("concurrency", "max_connections_per_ip", "retry_interval_seconds"):
+        if key in rate_limit and not _positive_int(rate_limit.get(key)):
+            reasons.append(f"{key} must be a positive integer")
+    if "retry_interval_seconds" in rate_limit and not _is_http_url(rate_limit.get("retry_citation")):

+    return reasons

+
+def _auth_reasons(source: dict) -> list[str]:

+    if source.get("auth_required") is not False:
+        reasons.append("requires auth")
+    access = source.get("access")
+    if access is not None and access != "unauthenticated":
+        reasons.append("requires auth")
+    for key in AUTH_FLAG_KEYS:
+        if source.get(key) is True:
+            reasons.append("requires auth")
+    for key in SECRET_KEYS:
+        value = source.get(key)
+        if value not in (None, "", False):

+    quota = source.get("rate_limit")
+    if isinstance(quota, dict) and quota.get("quota") == "authenticated":
+        reasons.append("requires auth")
+    return reasons
+
+
+def _evasion_reasons(source: dict) -> list[str]:
+    reasons = []
+    blobs = [source]
+    rate_limit = source.get("rate_limit")
+    if isinstance(rate_limit, dict):
+        blobs.append(rate_limit)
+    for blob in blobs:
+        for key in EVASION_KEYS:
+            if blob.get(key) is True:
+                reasons.append("rate-limit evasion is refused")
+    return reasons
+
+
+def _result(source_id: str | None, reasons: list[str]) -> dict:
+    unique = list(dict.fromkeys(reasons))
+    return {"id": source_id, "ok": not unique, "reasons": unique}
+
+
+def _is_http_url(value) -> bool:
+    if not isinstance(value, str):
+        return False
+    text = value.strip()
+    lowered = text.lower()
+    if not (lowered.startswith("https://") or lowered.startswith("http://")):
+        return False
+    if any(char.isspace() for char in text):
+        return False
+    return not _url_has_userinfo(text)
+
+
+def _url_has_userinfo(value) -> bool:
+    if not isinstance(value, str) or "://" not in value:
+        return False
+    host = value.split("://", 1)[1].split("/", 1)[0]
+    return "@" in host
+
+
+def _positive_number(value) -> bool:
+    return isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0
+
+
+def _positive_int(value) -> bool:
+    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0
+
+
+def summarize(results: list[dict]) -> dict:
+    accepted = [item["id"] for item in results if item["ok"]]
+    rejected = [item for item in results if not item["ok"]]
+    return {
+        "accepted": len(accepted),
+        "rejected": len(rejected),
+        "accepted_ids": accepted,
+        "rejected_ids": [item["id"] for item in rejected],
+    }
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Check a SHEPHERD allowlist offline.")
+    parser.add_argument("path", nargs="?", type=Path, default=default_allowlist_path())
+    parser.add_argument("--report", action="store_true", help="Print accepted and rejected counts.")

+            else:

+        print(f"accepted {summary['accepted']} rejected {summary['rejected']}")
+    return 0 if summary["rejected"] == 0 else 1
+
+
